title: Look Again: How We Check
subtitle: The Garden Welcome Sign
author: Maria Smith
mission: Help the friends rebuild and check one welcome sign so the garden gate can open.
stable_item_rule: Every repeated sign picture, corner mark, measuring tile and answer mark uses one stable OpenMoji 16.0 emoji asset. Generated illustration supplies settings, characters and one-off story action only.

pages.heading: Look Again: How We Check
pages.text: The Garden Welcome Sign
pages.alt: Mia, Tavi, Sol and Ivo stand at a bright garden gate beside a welcome sign made from four clear emoji pictures.

pages.heading: Look Again: How We Check
pages.text:
A Star Rooms Adventure · Book 4

Written by Maria Smith
SFT Open Education · Early Years · ages 3–5
Review edition 2.0.0 · CC BY 4.0
pages.subtext: This is a complete picture-book adventure. It works without the companion game. Final publication awaits Maria Smith’s approval.
pages.alt: A simple title page shows the four stable welcome-sign emoji pictures: sunflower, bee, apple and boot.

pages.heading: The trail finds a gate
pages.text:
Last time, you helped Mia, Sol and Tavi mend the moon-and-sun light trail.

The trail now led them to a garden gate. The gate was shut.
pages.alt: The repaired light trail reaches a closed garden gate. Mia, Tavi and Sol stop beside it.

pages.heading: One clear job
pages.text:
A blank sign stood by the gate. A small plan showed four pictures.

“Let’s make the sign match the plan,” said Mia. “Then we can check it.”
pages.alt: A picture plan shows sunflower with sun, bee with moon, apple with leaf and boot with star. A second sign has four empty spaces beside the closed gate.

pages.heading: Meet Ivo
pages.text:
A moss-green friend hurried over. He carried a big round lens.

“I’m Ivo,” he said. “I look again when something needs checking. May I help?”
pages.alt: Ivo joins Mia, Tavi and Sol beside the closed gate. His large round lens is easy to see.

pages.heading: First, look
pages.text:
Ivo held up the picture plan.

“Look slowly,” said Tavi. “What picture is beside the moon?”
pages.alt: The full emoji picture plan is visible beside the closed gate. The moon corner contains a bee.

pages.heading: Find the moon corner
pages.text:
Find the MOON on the plan.

Which picture is beside it? Point to SUNFLOWER, BEE, APPLE or BOOT.
pages.subtext: Look at the plan before you choose. The next page explains the answer.
pages.alt: The plan stays visible above four large emoji choices: sunflower, bee, apple and boot.

pages.heading: You found the bee
pages.text:
The BEE is beside the MOON.

You answered from something you could see. That is an observation: saying what you can see now.
pages.alt: The moon and bee emoji cards are outlined together and labelled MOON and BEE beside the closed gate.

pages.heading: Four cards to place
pages.text:
Ivo opened his bag. Out came a sunflower, a bee, an apple and a boot.

The blank sign waited. The plan stayed where everyone could see it.
pages.alt: Four stable emoji picture cards wait beside the visible plan and blank sign.

pages.heading: Which sign matches?
pages.text:
Look at the plan. Then look at signs A, B and C.

Which sign puts every picture beside the same corner mark?
pages.subtext: Point to A, B or C. Check all four places before you turn the page.
pages.alt: Three complete emoji signs are shown. Only sign B exactly matches the visible picture plan.

pages.heading: Sign B matches
pages.text:
Sign B has all four pictures in the same places as the plan.

The friends used the plan while they built. Now they had a sign they could check again.
pages.alt: Plan and sign B appear side by side with matching sunflower, bee, apple and boot emoji positions.

pages.heading: Curtain up, curtain down
pages.text:
Ivo showed the plan once more. Then a golden curtain covered it.

“Can we remember the four places?” asked Sol.
pages.alt: The emoji plan is shown beside a golden curtain that will cover it.

pages.heading: What was beside the star?
pages.text:
The plan is covered.

Which picture was beside the STAR: BEE, APPLE or BOOT?
pages.subtext: It is fine to say “I’m not sure.” Turn the page to look again.
pages.alt: A covered plan appears above three emoji choices: bee, apple and boot.

pages.heading: Look again
pages.text:
Ivo opened the curtain. The BOOT was beside the STAR.

Looking again is how we check a memory. “I wasn’t sure” is a useful answer before we look.
pages.alt: The open plan highlights the boot beside the star emoji corner.

pages.heading: Spot the two changes
pages.text:
Sol made a first try from memory. Keep it beside the plan.

Which two pictures changed places? Point to both.
pages.subtext: Check each corner. The first try stays visible on the next page.
pages.alt: The plan and Sol’s first try are side by side. Bee and boot have swapped places; sunflower and apple stayed put.

pages.heading: Bee and boot swapped
pages.text:
BEE and BOOT changed places. SUNFLOWER and APPLE stayed put.

The friends kept Sol’s first try. It helped them see exactly what needed fixing.
pages.alt: Bee and boot are outlined on the two retained emoji signs. The unchanged pictures remain visible.

pages.heading: Where did the change begin?
pages.text:
Ivo kept one card for each move Sol made. Read the cards from 1 to 4.

Which is the first card that does not follow the plan?
pages.subtext: Point to 1, 2, 3 or 4. Start at the beginning.
pages.alt: Four ordered emoji step cards show Sol placing sunflower, apple, boot and bee. Step 3 is the first placement that differs from the plan.

pages.heading: Step 3 changed first
pages.text:
Steps 1 and 2 followed the plan. Step 3 put BOOT beside MOON.

That was the first change. Keeping the steps in order showed where the mix-up began.
pages.alt: All four step cards remain visible. Step 3 is clearly outlined as the first changed move.

pages.heading: Repair the moon corner
pages.text:
The moon corner has the wrong picture.

Which card belongs there: SUNFLOWER, BEE, APPLE or BOOT?
pages.subtext: Use the picture plan. Point before you turn the page.
pages.alt: Sol’s retained try highlights the moon corner. Four stable emoji picture choices appear below.

pages.heading: The pictures match
pages.text:
BEE went back beside MOON. BOOT went back beside STAR.

Now the rebuilt sign matched the plan. Next, the friends had to see if the sign would fit the gate.
pages.alt: The repaired emoji sign matches the picture plan in all four positions.

pages.heading: How wide is the sign?
pages.text:
WIDTH means the distance from one side to the other.

Count the yellow tiles across the sign. Is it 3, 4 or 5 tiles wide?
pages.subtext: Touch each equal emoji tile once as you count across.
pages.alt: Four equal yellow square emoji tiles run from the left edge of the sign to the right edge. Choices are 3, 4 and 5.

pages.heading: Four tiles wide
pages.text:
The sign is 4 tiles wide. The four-tile space between the hooks is the same width. It fits.

This check answered one question: how wide is it?
pages.alt: Four yellow square emoji tiles align across the sign and between the gate hooks. Both widths are labelled 4.

pages.heading: How tall is the sign?
pages.text:
HEIGHT means the distance from the bottom to the top.

Count the blue tiles up the sign. Is it 2, 3 or 4 tiles tall?
pages.subtext: Count from the bottom upwards. Width and height are different questions.
pages.alt: Three equal blue square emoji tiles run from the bottom edge of the sign to the top edge. Choices are 2, 3 and 4.

pages.heading: Three tiles tall
pages.text:
The sign is 3 tiles tall. The three-tile space at the gate is the same height. It fits.

The first tiles checked side to side. These tiles checked bottom to top.
pages.alt: Three blue square emoji tiles align vertically with the sign and the gate space. Both heights are labelled 3.

pages.heading: Ivo checks without peeking
pages.text:
The team covered its finished sign. Ivo used the same plan and a fresh set of picture cards.

He made his own sign without seeing theirs.
pages.alt: A hedge hides the team sign while Ivo builds a fresh emoji sign from the same visible plan.

pages.heading: Same or different?
pages.text:
Now both signs are uncovered. Look at every corner.

Are the two signs the SAME or DIFFERENT?
pages.subtext: Point to SAME or DIFFERENT. Check all four pictures.
pages.alt: The team sign and Ivo’s sign appear side by side. All four emoji pictures are in the same places.

pages.heading: Ivo’s sign matches
pages.text:
The two signs are the same. Ivo did not copy the team’s answer. He made his own check, and it matched.

A check can agree, show a difference, or show that we need to look again.
pages.alt: Four green check emoji marks pair the matching positions on the team sign and Ivo’s sign.

pages.heading: Choose the picture check
pages.text:
Question 1: Do the pictures match the plan?

Which card answers that question: PLAN AND SIGN, WIDTH TILES, or HEIGHT TILES?
pages.subtext: Choose the card that looked at picture places.
pages.alt: Three clear record cards show a plan beside a sign, four horizontal tiles and three vertical tiles.

pages.heading: The plan checked the pictures
pages.text:
The PLAN AND SIGN card answers the picture question.

The width tiles answered width. The height tiles answered height. Ivo’s own sign checked the result without copying.
pages.alt: Four illustrated record cards are labelled pictures, width, height and Ivo’s own check.

pages.heading: Is every check ready?
pages.text:
Look at the four question cards. Each one has a clear answer.

Is the sign ready for the gate: YES or NOT YET?
pages.subtext: Check pictures, width, height and Ivo’s own sign before choosing.
pages.alt: Four question cards each carry a green check emoji. Two answer choices say YES and NOT YET.

pages.heading: The garden gate opens
pages.text:
YES. Every question had its own checked answer. The pictures matched. The width fit. The height fit. Ivo’s sign matched too.

The gate opened, and the morning visitors cheered.
pages.alt: The garden gate stands open behind the checked emoji welcome sign. The four friends celebrate.

pages.heading: You learned how to check
pages.text:
You looked before answering. You kept a try that did not match. You followed its steps, fixed the first change, measured one direction at a time, and used a second sign made without copying.

Checking matters because it helps us explain what we saw, find a change and decide what to do next. Beyond the garden, a new Star Door began to glow.
pages.alt: The four friends stand by the open garden gate and correct emoji sign while a distant Star Door glows.
